articles.title: Missing alt vs empty alt: a one-minute image check for landing pages

articles.body: Landing pages are full of images: hero shots, icons, dividers, screenshots. Two different mistakes with alt are easy to make, and a quick look at the source finds both. The check View the page source and search for <img . For each image, ask what it is for. It carries information (a product screenshot, a chart, a logo that is also a link): alt should say what a person who can't see it needs to know. It is decoration (a flourish, a background shape, an icon next to text that already says the same thing): use an empty alt="" . There is no alt attribute at all : that is the one to fix first.

articles.title: Autonomous LLM Agents as Dynamic Decision Nodes in Temporal Sagas
articles.excerpt: Modern core banking platforms are increasingly adopting generative AI and Large Language Model (LLM) agents to handle complex operational reasoning—such as assessing unstructured trade finance documen…
articles.body: Modern core banking platforms are increasingly adopting generative AI and Large Language Model (LLM) agents to handle complex operational reasoning—such as assessing unstructured trade finance documents, triaging complex fraud cases, and resolving cross-border exception processing. However, introducing autonomous AI agents into core banking workflows presents a fundamental architectural contradiction: Temporal Sagas demand absolute determinism, whereas LLM reasoning is inherently non-deterministic. Temporal workflows achieve fault tolerance through event-sourced execution replay. If a workflow definition behaves non-deterministically during history replay, execution drifts, state corruption occurs, and replay validation fails.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 20, 1970: The Soviet Union launches last-ever Zond moon mission
articles.excerpt: On Oct. 20, 1970, the Soviet Union launched the Zond 8 spacecraft on a mission to the moon. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Oct. 20, 1970, the Soviet Union launched the Zond 8 spacecraft on a mission to the moon. This was the last mission in the Zond program. After the first three Zond missions explored Venus and Mars , the next ones were circumlunar missions that flew around the moon before returning to Earth. Although there was no crew on board, the Zond spacecraft was designed with cosmonauts in mind. The Zond missions served as test flights for the Soviet Union's plans to send cosmonauts to the moon. But those plans for crewed flights never came to fruition. This was partly because the U.S. had already put astronauts on the moon , but also because the Zond missions had a lot of technical problems. Zond 8 was considered a success — even though its guidance system malfunctioned on the way back to Earth.
